title: Visualizing cytoplasmic ATP in C. elegans larvae using PercevalHR
protocol: Grow animals expressing PercevalHR on the standard OP50 bacteria feeding strain for 2–3 generations without starvation before imaging.
Select mid-L3 larval worms from the plate using a dissecting microscope based on vulval morphology.
Pick mid-L3 larval worms from the plate with a platinum wire.
Mount picked worms onto an agar pad on a microscope slide.
Use differential interference contrast (DIC) microscopy and high magnification on a compound microscope to identify the AC and its stage of invasion.
Grow animals on RNAi bacteria (HT115) expressing empty vector control for 2–3 generations without starvation before transferring onto RNAi conditions for synchronized egg-laying.
Transfer animals to blank NGM plates with no bacteria for 45–60 min to clear HT115 empty vector bacteria.
Transfer animals to experimental RNAi plates.
Set up the point-scanning confocal setup using a Zeiss 63× Plan-Apochromat 1.4NA oil immersion objective.
Configure Channel 1: Excitation 488 nm for PercevalHR image acquisition.
Configure Channel 2: Excitation 405 nm for PercevalHR image acquisition.
Set the emission range from 490 to 553 nm.
Anesthetize animals expressing PercevalHR with 5 mM levamisole for 15–20 minutes.
Prepare a noble agar pad by compressing a drop of warm 5% noble agar between two clean slides spaced with guide-slides.
Transfer anesthetized worms to the prepared noble agar pad using a mouth pipette.
Remove excess buffer from around the transferred worms.
Place a 22 mm × 22 mm coverslip at an angle over the worms and agar pad carefully to avoid creating bubbles.
Seal the edges of the coverslip using warm VALAP solution applied with a fine paintbrush.
Leave two small gaps in the VALAP seal to allow gas-exchange.
Anesthetize C. elegans in levamisole.
Dilute 200 mM levamisole stock to a 5 mM working stock in 100 μL of M9 buffer.
Transfer 20–30 animals into the well of a glass spot plate using a platinum wire pick.
Swirl the pick gently and move it in and out of the buffer slowly to transfer the animals without introducing excess E. coli into the buffer.
Allow animals to anesthetize at room temperature for 15–20 min.
Mount C. elegans onto agar pad.
Prepare a 5% (weight/volume) noble agar pad that is slightly smaller than a 22 mm × 22 mm coverslip.
Transfer 20–30 anesthetized animals onto the prepared agar pad using a mouth pipette.
Remove excess M9 buffer using the edge of a Kimwipe or mouth pipette.
Gently place the coverslip over the animals on the agar pad starting with one edge and then slowly lowering the coverslip until the opposite edge rests on top of the pad.
Seal the edges of the coverslip using a fine paintbrush and VALAP, leaving two small gaps on opposing sides for gas-exchange.
Mount animals expressing PercevalHR onto a slide for imaging.
Place the slide on the microscope stage with anesthetized L3 staged animals expressing PercevalHR.
Find L3 staged worms using low magnification (10× or 20× air objective).
Mark X-Y coordinates in Zen Black or Micromanager.
Switch to higher magnification (63× or 100× oil-immersion objective) and use DIC microscopy to determine the precise developmental stage of the AC.
Determine the developmental stage using the number of P6.p vulval precursor cell descendants.
Bring the central plane of the AC into focus with a low laser power at 488 nm.
Acquire PercevalHR images.
Set both lasers to their required laser power for the Zeiss LSM 880.
Use 22% laser power for the 488 nm laser and 8% for the 405 nm laser on a Zeiss LSM 880.
Acquire fluorescence signal from ATP-bound and ADP-bound channels simultaneously through the emission filter stated in microscopy settings.
Set both channels to their required laser powers and exposure settings for a Zeiss AxioImager equipped with an ImagEM EMCCD camera and VersaLase(4) laser system.
Use 18% laser power and 250 ms exposure for the ATP-bound channel and 488 nm laser.
Use 35% laser power and 400 ms exposure for the ADP-bound channel and 405 nm laser.
Acquire confocal z-stack in both channels.
Determine the ATP:ADP ratio by dividing fluorescence intensity of pixels in the ATP-bound channel (488 nm) by intensity of pixels in the ADP-bound channel (405 nm).
Open .tiff files directly in Fiji.
Import images using the Bio-Formats Importer plugin for proprietary file formats such as .czi.
Split 488 nm and 405 nm channels apart using "Image > Color > Split Channels".
Ensure that the two images have different names or unique identifiers (e.g., C1 and C2).
Create sum projections of each channel separately if data were collected as z-stacks.
Divide the pixel values in the 488 nm channel by the pixel values in the 405 nm channel using Image Calculator function “Process > Image Calculator”.
Select the “Operation” dropdown menu and choose “Divide”.
Choose the 488 nm image as Image 1.
Choose the 405 nm image as Image 2.
Check the boxes for “Create new window” and “32-bit (float) result” to obtain the final ratiometric ATP:ADP image.

Optional: Adjust the displayed minimum and maximum pixel values in the ratiometric image using “Image > Adjust > Brightness and Contrast > Set” if the range of pixel values does not cover the full bit-depth of the detector.
Set the same displayed minimum and maximum pixel values for all images within an experiment for publication purposes to ensure accurate comparison.
Represent the image as a spectral heatmap using “Image > Lookup Tables > 16 color” for better visualization of heterogeneities in cellular distribution of ATP:ADP ratio.
Draw a region of interest (ROI) around the whole cell using the freehand selection tool.
Measure the mean pixel values within the selected ROI.
Use the same ROI to measure the mean background pixel values away from the PercevalHR expressing cell.
Calculate the final ATP:ADP ratio value for each cell as [mean intracellular pixel intensity] – [mean background pixel intensity].
Draw ROIs around the regions to be compared, such as basal vs. apical areas.
Measure the mean pixel values within each ROI.
Compute the background corrected ATP:ADP values for each region using the background value determined above.
Represent the relative enrichment of one region compared to another as a ratio of their final ATP:ADP ratio values.
